facts.F8: A note written with authentication off has no author
facts.F80: Maintainer, 2026-11-26, answering who may change or delete a note: "same as delivery notes".
facts.F81: The first wording said any writer may change any note while authentication is off. Delivery notes decide by the note instead: a note nobody signed belongs to nobody, and a signed note stays its author's.
facts.F82: A signed note stays its author's after authentication is switched off
facts.F83: a note on a report signed by a user while authentication was on, and authentication is now off
facts.F84: a user with write access on the owner tries to change or delete the note
facts.F85: the user sees no control to change or delete that note, and a direct request to do so is refused
facts.F86: A frozen, read-only state for notes: reports have no archived state, unlike Deliveries, so no note is ever frozen.
facts.F87: Changing and deleting a note follows Delivery notes, decided by the note: a signed note only by its author; a note nobody signed (written with authentication off) by any user with write access on the owner (maintainer, 2026-11-26: "same as delivery notes").
facts.F88: Notes belong to the report, not to its template, so every report type has them (ADO #6564: "a generic concept for all report types"); how large the Team is goes in as note text (DIVERGE recommendation; the maintainer was asked to object to this direction and answered with the four DISCUSS answers and "Start discuss", 2026-11-26).
facts.F89: The author name is the name as it stood when the note was written, as for Delivery notes, so a note does not re-label itself when someone is renamed or removed (maintainer, 2026-11-26: "similar to deliveries", "same as delivery notes").
facts.F90: A user with write access adds a note to a report in the live report and sees it listed, newest first, with the day it was written and their name (no name when authentication is off); a note without text is not saved; deleting the report deletes its notes.
facts.F91: The author changes or deletes their own note, others cannot, and a note nobody signed may be changed or deleted by any writer.
